\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عیدی} ('eydi)}{عیدی ('eydi)}]{\fa{عیدی} ('eydi) — New Year money, a holiday gift}

\label{lesson:FA-C340-eydi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for oleaster, then the Persian for a goldfish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عیدی}}
\textbf{\fa{عیدی}} (\emph{'eydi}) — \textquotedblleft{}New Year money, a holiday gift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگ} \fa{به} \fa{همه} \fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{عیدی} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedarbozorg be hame-ye bachche-hâ 'eydi dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandfather gave all the children their New Year money.
\end{quote}

Usually crisp new banknotes, given by the elders. \emph{'Eydi gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to get one's New Year gift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'eydi} adds the Persian suffix \emph{-i} to \emph{'eyd} \textquotedblleft{}festival\textquotedblright{}, which is borrowed from Arabic \emph{'īd} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'eydi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'eydi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'eydi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for oleaster, then the Persian for a goldfish, then say \emph{'eydi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید} (did o bâzdid)}{دید و بازدید (did o bâzdid)}]{\fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید} (did o bâzdid) — a round of visits (at the New Year)}

\label{lesson:FA-C340-did-o-bazdid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a goldfish, then the Persian for New Year money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید}}
\textbf{\fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید}} (\emph{did o bâzdid}) — \textquotedblleft{}a round of visits (at the New Year)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{روزهای} \fa{عید} \fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید} \fa{داریم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar ruz-hâ-ye 'eyd did o bâzdid dârim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
During the New Year holidays we go round visiting family.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}seeing and seeing back\textquotedblright{}: you visit, then they return the visit. The elders are visited first.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{did} \textquotedblleft{}a seeing\textquotedblright{} and \emph{bâzdid} \textquotedblleft{}a return visit\textquotedblright{} (\emph{bâz} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} + \emph{did}) are both built on the past stem of the native verb \emph{didan} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{did o bâzdid}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{did o bâzdid}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{did o bâzdid}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a goldfish, then the Persian for New Year money, then say \emph{did o bâzdid} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{دید} \fa{و} \fa{بازدید} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A round of visits (at the New Year)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آیین} (âyin)}{آیین (âyin)}]{\fa{آیین} (âyin) — a rite, a ritual}

\label{lesson:FA-C340-ayin}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for New Year money, then the Persian for a round of visits.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آیین}}
\textbf{\fa{آیین}} (\emph{âyin}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rite, a ritual\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پریدن} \fa{از} \fa{روی} \fa{آتش} \fa{یک} \fa{آیین} \fa{قدیمی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Paridan az ru-ye âtash yek âyin-e qadimi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Jumping over a fire is an old ritual.
\end{quote}

It also means \textquotedblleft{}a religion, a creed\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Âyin-e Nowruz} \textquotedblleft{}the Nowruz rites\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âyin} is a native Persian word that EtymDB glosses \textquotedblleft{}custom\textquotedblright{} with no parent; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{ēwēn}, \textquotedblleft{}manner, custom\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رسم} (rasm)}{رسم (rasm)}]{\fa{رسم} (rasm) — a custom, a tradition}

\label{lesson:FA-C340-rasm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a round of visits, then the Persian for a rite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رسم}}
\textbf{\fa{رسم}} (\emph{rasm}) — \textquotedblleft{}a custom, a tradition\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{خانواده} \fa{ما} \fa{رسم} \fa{است} \fa{که} \fa{شب} \fa{عید} \fa{همه} \fa{دور} \fa{هم} \fa{جمع} \fa{شوند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar khânevâde-ye mâ rasm ast ke shab-e 'eyd hame dor-e ham jam' shavand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In our family it is the custom for everyone to get together on New Year's Eve.
\end{quote}

Broken plural \emph{rosum}: \emph{rasm-o rosum} \textquotedblleft{}customs and traditions\textquotedblright{}. In Arabic the word means \textquotedblleft{}a drawing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rasm} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{rasm}, \textquotedblleft{}a drawing, a picture\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); in Persian it came to mean a custom, a traced-out way of doing things.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسپند} (espand)}{اسپند (espand)}]{\fa{اسپند} (espand) — wild rue (seeds burned for luck)}

\label{lesson:FA-C340-espand}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rite, then the Persian for a custom.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسپند}}
\textbf{\fa{اسپند}} (\emph{espand}) — \textquotedblleft{}wild rue (seeds burned for luck)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{برای} \fa{ما} \fa{اسپند} \fa{دود} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdarbozorgam barâ-ye mâ espand dud kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother burned wild rue for us.
\end{quote}

The seeds are burned on hot coals against the evil eye, at weddings and at the New Year.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{espand} \textquotedblleft{}wild rue\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian word, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{spand}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
